parallel.requirements: Recognized the required ESM .mjs Node implementation, local-only imports, manual parsing for --a/--b/--c, OMD behavior, Python repr formatting, and output placement in /output.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: The parent owned implementation, integration, verification, and delivery. It delegated executable-behavior probing to one child while also performing parent-side probes.
parallel.implementation: Implemented python_repr.mjs, ordered_multi_dict.mjs, arg_parser.mjs, and test6.mjs. It modeled duplicate OMD entries, getlist, unique keys, latest-value items, and argparse-like errors.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: The parent created a coherent four-file hierarchy with local ESM imports and delivered test6.mjs plus library modules; artifact validation later copied those exact files.
parallel.verification: The parent compared normal and special-string outputs byte-for-byte and checked missing arguments, unknown arguments, help, repeated options, and negative-number-like values.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: Official evaluation still failed 5 of 157 cases. The visible common risk is that final acceptance allowed help/error usage to say test6.mjs instead of exact executable-style program naming.

serial.requirements: Recognized the same required pure Node ESM .mjs port, local module hierarchy, manual argv parsing, OMD semantics, Python repr formatting, and /output delivery.
serial.plan_and_ownership: A single serial agent owned the full pipeline: observe executable behavior, implement formatter/parser/OMD modules, verify, clean temporary artifacts, and finalize.
serial.implementation: Implemented pythonRepr.mjs, orderedMultiDict.mjs, argparseLike.mjs, index.mjs, and test6.mjs with similar OMD, repr, and parser coverage to the parallel run.
serial.integration_and_delivery: The serial run assembled an internally consistent five-file ESM hierarchy with a re-export index and the required test6.mjs entrypoint; artifact validation copied those files.
serial.verification: It performed more local edge-case probing than the parallel run, including help aliases, unknown options, Unicode, controls, repeated flags, and a scripted comparison set that passed.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: Official evaluation still failed 5 of 157 cases. Its final response also treated the program-name change in usage/error text as expected, matching the parallel shortfall.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parallel run worked from the same prompt requiring ESM .mjs files, manual argv parsing, local-only imports, OMD behavior, and exact printed output.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial run worked from the identical prompt and tracked the same requirements for ESM, argument parsing, OMD output, no npm dependencies, and /output files.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No material requirement-recognition difference is visible; both later missed or accepted the same program-name parity issue for help/error output.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parent created a three-step plan, spawned one child to probe executable behavior, and kept implementation plus final verification ownership in the parent.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial run had multi-agent disabled and one agent owned probing, implementation, verification, cleanup, and delivery without delegation.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel split off behavior discovery but did not split implementation ownership; serial performed the same work locally.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The child received the task context through the spawned thread and returned a concise final behavioral report about CLI output, errors, repeated options, and OMD semantics.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial run gathered the same interface facts directly by executing the reference program and inspecting outputs before implementing.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had a parent-child handoff, but it was available early and consistent with the parent's own probes; no missing or conflicting interface contract is evidenced.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel added formatter, OMD, parser, and entry modules, then patched the parser's negative-number rule after detecting a drift for -1.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial added formatter, OMD, parser, index, and entry modules in one local patch and used a similar parser rule for option-like tokens.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The file naming and presence of an index barrel differed, but both produced equivalent functional structures and the same official score.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The only child completed normally and its final result reached the parent before the implementation patch and verification sequence.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: There was no child result lifecycle in serial; all observations and decisions stayed in the single main trajectory.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel introduced a child result handoff but did not leave it trapped, cancelled, unjoined, or unused in a way that caused a realized adverse consequence.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Only the parent wrote the deliverable files; the child performed executable probes and returned text findings, with no evidence of shared-workspace file writes or collisions.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial run wrote its own final file hierarchy locally, including an index module, and artifact validation copied the expected entry plus libraries.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel did not suffer a shared-state merge problem; both runs assembled valid-looking ESM hierarchies with different file naming conventions.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel ran normal, special-string, parser-edge, negative-number, and byte-for-byte comparison checks and reported successful local verification.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial ran a broader local matrix, including help aliases, unknown arguments, Unicode/control repr, and a comparison script that reported all comparisons passed.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Serial verified more edge cases locally, but both accepted the same program-name variation in help/error text and both official evaluations failed 5 hidden cases.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel finished normally in about 380 agent seconds with one child and no host timeout, leaving enough time for implementation and verification.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial finished normally in about 314 agent seconds with no subagents and no host timeout, also leaving enough time for implementation and verification.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel used more tokens and elapsed time because of delegation and duplicated probing, but there is no evidence that budget pressure displaced required work.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The current completed official evaluations are not discordant: both parallel and serial have solution_passed false with 152 of 157 samples passed. The trajectories show very similar task solutions, and both final responses explicitly accept help/error text using test6.mjs as the program name rather than matching the reference executable name exactly. The parallel child-agent episode supplied useful probing information and returned before implementation closed, so it does not explain a worse parallel outcome.
parallel_contributors: Parallel delegated executable probing to one child while the parent retained implementation, integration, verification, and final delivery ownership.
The parent received the child's behavior report before writing and verifying the final files.
serial_contributors: Serial performed the same behavior discovery and implementation locally without any subagent handoff.
Serial ran a somewhat broader local CLI edge-case matrix, but still ended with the same official failure count.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Both runs treated program-name drift in usage/error output as expected, even though the task required command-line behavior and console output alignment.
Parallel used snake_case module names without an index barrel, while serial used camelCase module names and an index barrel; this did not change the official score relation.
evaluator_effects: The current status files expose aggregate pass counts but not individual failing testcase names, so the exact five failed samples cannot be isolated from the mounted evidence.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: no outcome difference; common ordinary implementation and acceptance gap

candidates.reason: The parallel parent explicitly owned and performed the implementation patch; the child was limited to behavior probing.
There were not multiple independently implemented components needing an unowned reconciliation step; the parent assembled the modules.
The parent created the required entrypoint and library files and artifact validation found test6.mjs in the final output tree.
The parent carried the pipeline from probing through implementation, verification, and final response; no end-to-end transition was ownerless.
Executable probing informed the work but did not block all productive implementation behind a mandatory serial gate with a delay consequence.
The child and parent probes overlapped, and implementation completed with verification; investigation did not create an incomplete or shortened closure phase.
The indispensable implementation path stayed with the parent and received active work; no auxiliary work starved implementation or verification.
Only one child was spawned, the run did not time out, and there is no direct evidence that fan-out consumed the finite budget before required closure work.
The child assignment was narrow executable-behavior probing and completed with a useful final report; no overbroad child scope left indispensable work unfinished.
The child performed the intended executable probing and returned relevant CLI and OMD findings; no known requirement omitted from the brief made its work unusable.
The child did not own an interoperating code component or file interface; it returned behavioral findings, so no cross-agent implementation contract was missing.
No known finding is shown disappearing between child and parent; the child's final report includes the material behavior observations it gathered.
The child handoff was concise enough to be inspectable, and the parent continued with implementation and verification instead of leaving it unconsumed.
The child reported observations from the same reference executable before implementation, not a superseded workspace or decision state.
The child's findings did not conflict with the parent's own probes in a way that remained unadjudicated at integration time.
The parent ran integrated local comparisons before finalizing; the remaining official failures are not tied to a parent-visible unresolved integrated mismatch from non-evaluator evidence.
There was no replacement child or repeated retry episode lacking inherited findings or current-file state.

candidates.reason: The child completed normally with a final report; no parent or workflow action stopped an active child before needed work was finalized.
The parent promoted and delivered the implementation before closure; there was no complete candidate left unpackaged or unplaced because finalization started too late.
The relevant implementation edits occurred before the final local comparisons; no child result or code change was merged only after verification without a post-merge check.
No delegated implementation was completed by a child; the only child provided probe findings, not code requiring adoption into the final implementation.
The child was not a verifier producing a trapped finding below the parent; its report returned to the parent before closure.
No required child failed, aborted, or was cancelled; there was no unfinished child scope that the parent needed to take over.
The child result was visible and aligned with the parent's later implementation and checks; the parent did not proceed inconsistently with an ignored result.
The parent did not wait until timeout or near-deadline without inspection; it actively probed, edited, verified, and finished without host timeout.
The child did not write a competing implementation path; there were no overlapping component designs requiring reconciliation.
Only the parent edited output files, and no live agents are shown concurrently editing the same source or configuration file.
No actor replaced non-entry source produced or owned by another live actor; the child produced findings rather than source files.
The parent created the entrypoint and no other live actor owned or replaced the required submitted deliverable.
There was no broad cleanup, rebuild, or promotion replacing another actor's final-tree work or provenance.
Although the workspace was shared, only the parent wrote implementation files, so no unstable-state or provenance problem from unisolated multi-writes materialized.
No generated child file, fixture, cache, temporary path, or tool output was consumed by another actor as stable reference input.

suppressed_same_chain_candidates: The single child probing episode was considered against child-brief, handoff, join, monitoring, and load-imbalance labels but produced no realized adverse parallel consequence.
